sources.entry: 2FAuth - Manage your Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) accounts and generate their security codes. (Demo) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Docker
2FAuth | Web app to manage your two-factor authentication (2FA) accounts

summary.one_liner: 2FAuth is a self-hosted web app for managing two-factor authentication accounts and generating their TOTP, HOTP and Steam Guard security codes.
summary.what_it_does: 2FAuth stores your 2FA accounts in a standalone database and generates one-time codes for them, aiming to be a web-based alternative to apps like Google Authenticator. Accounts can be added by scanning a QR code or through a manual form, and they can be organized into groups and edited, including imported ones. It generates TOTP and HOTP codes as well as Steam Guard codes, and follows RFC 4226 and RFC 6238 via the OTPHP PHP library. It supports importing from 2FAuth JSON, Google Auth QR codes, Aegis Auth, and 2FAS Auth exports. The README describes a multi-user setup with configurable registration, optional security key sign-in, optional database encryption, and auto logout. The interface is available in English and French.
use_cases: generate two-factor login codes on a desktop browser
back up and restore 2FA accounts in a database
import accounts from Google Authenticator or Aegis
share a 2FA code manager among multiple users
how_to_run: Follow the self-hosted server guide in the README (requires Laravel server requirements)
Or use the Docker (cli) installation guide
Or use the Docker (compose) installation guide
Or use the Heroku installation guide
Demo available with credentials demo@2fauth.app / demo
notable: Displays one account's code at a time rather than all accounts with countdowns
Standalone database that is easy to back up and restore
Supports TOTP, HOTP and Steam Guard codes
Optional encryption of sensitive database data and security key sign-in
Imports from Google Auth, Aegis and 2FAS Auth exports
caveats: Encryption is off by default, and the README strongly recommends backing up the APP_KEY value when it is enabled
Setup requires a Laravel-compatible PHP server or Docker; the README gives no platform specifics beyond these guides
